rationale: I read the complete held EO 11979 (42 FR 16771, Mar. 28, 1977): its only operative sentence amends sec. 1(b) of EO 11832 (as amended by EO 11889) to raise the National Commission on the Observance of International Women's Year, 1975 to not more than 45 members; it has no other section, no own term and no savings clause, so it is a pure amendment whose entire effect lives inside EO 11832. EO 11980 (Mar. 29, 1977) then further amended the same sec. 1(b), changing 45 to 42 members; that is an amendment of the amended text, not an ending. I read the complete held EO 12050 (43 FR 14431, Apr. 4, 1978, 'Establishing a National Advisory Committee for Women'): sec. 8 states 'Executive Order No. 11126, as amended, and Executive Order No. 11832, as amended, are revoked' with no exception, delay or savings clause, and sec. 4(c) sets up a different committee. The revocation of EO 11832 'as amended' removes the parent text that EO 11979 amended, leaving nothing of EO 11979 to operate; EO 11979 is not named, which is why the machine ACT row shows names_target=false and scope whole_via_parent, and I rely on the parent-as-amended wording and not on an express naming. D6 self-check: the later events are the EO 11980 amendment (before the revocation, and it changed the 45 figure to 42, not reviving anything) and the EO 12050 revocation; a corpus search for 11979 finds only EO 11979 itself plus unrelated page-number hits (EO 9372, 9617, 10296), so no later order revived the Commission or re-enacted the membership clause. No own earlier term applies. Provisional NO hypothesis only.
